cards.title: backlog: vehicles
cards.body:
from docs/BACKLOG.md (Vehicles). 11 of 15 already in the game.

- [x] Drivable hatchback and SUV on simplified Shitbox Rally physics: engine torque curve, gears, clutch, wheel slip, weight transfer, backfires
- [x] One click to get in or out; calm and combat versions of getting in and out
- [x] One-click drive to a destination along roads and open ground, with the AI driver avoiding obstacles
- [x] Firing from inside through open windows at realistic angles (no shooting through your own pillar or roof)
- [x] Vehicle armor by panel: engine block and wheels as cover, doors as concealment (driven cars too: checked per seat)
- [x] Tires shot out: a flat drags the car to that side and drops grip
- [x] Radiators and engines shot: overheating, smoke, then a dead engine
- [x] Ramming: doors, fences and people (with injury); men on foot get out of the way of a car they see or hear
- [x] Dismount drills: everyone out on the far side, then down behind the engine block and the wheels
- [ ] Mounted LMG on the SUV roof, with a gunner seat
- [x] Passengers' wounds from rounds through the body panels
- [x] Headlights at night, brake lights, interior light when a door opens
- [ ] Engine sound from the Shitbox engine model, drivetrain whine, gear changes
- [ ] Vehicle chatter: "STEP ON IT", "DRIVER'S HIT"
- [ ] Burnouts and handbrake turns for the player driving directly

cards.title: backlog: soldiers and ai
cards.body:
from docs/BACKLOG.md (Soldiers and AI). 5 of 35 already in the game.

- [ ] Suppression that actually keeps heads down: suppressed troops won't peek
- [ ] Leaders: a team leader who gives the orders, and the team falls apart a bit if he dies
- [x] Morale per team: casualties, being flanked and losing the leader lead to falling back or surrendering
- [ ] Better flanking: use cover-to-cover routes out of the enemy's sight
- [ ] Fire and maneuver at squad level: one team suppresses, the other moves
- [ ] Grenade cooking for timing
- [ ] Grenades thrown through windows and over walls with arcs
- [ ] Picking up ammo from the dead and from friends ("throw me a mag")
- [ ] Sharing ammo inside the team automatically
- [ ] Weapon malfunctions (rare), cleared with a tap-rack
- [ ] Weapon pickup: grab an enemy's rifle when your own is empty or broken
- [ ] Fatigue and stamina: sprints run out; aim gets worse after running
- [ ] Heat and cold over long missions
- [ ] Hearing damage after explosions indoors (deaf for a while: missed callouts)
- [ ] Night adaptation: eyes adjust over a minute after the lights go out
- [ ] Personal skills per soldier (marksmanship, CQB, medical, explosives) used by the sim
- [ ] Veterancy: skills grow with time in the field
- [ ] Individual fear: some freeze, some charge
- [ ] Friendly fire awareness: check fire when a friend steps into the line
- [ ] Civilians that flee, hide, or panic into the line of fire
- [ ] Hostages: held, used as shields, rescued
- [x] Surrender and detainees: flex-cuffs, search, move to a collection point
- [ ] Enemy feints and ambushes
- [ ] Enemy that retreats inside the house to a fallback room
- [ ] Barricaded rooms: furniture against doors
- [ ] Booby traps and tripwires on doors
- [ ] IEDs on roads, found by careful movement or drones
- [ ] Snipers relocating after a shot
- [x] AI using smoke to cross open ground
- [ ] AI using drones to spot (both sides)
- [x] Counter-sniper drills: find the shooter by crack-thump and suppress
- [ ] Medics triaging several casualties by severity
- [ ] CASEVAC to a vehicle and out
- [x] Buddy carry (fireman's carry) for longer moves
- [ ] Better wounded behavior: crawling to cover, calling for help, playing dead

cards.title: backlog: realism pass (next)
cards.body:
from docs/BACKLOG.md (Realism pass (next)). 5 of 35 already in the game.

- [x] Wounds by organ, bleed rates by vessel, tourniquets, packing, self-aid, care under fire
- [x] Real throw distances, 4.5 s frag fuses, cooking close in
- [x] Suppression and stress by class; untrained troops spray and stay exposed
- [ ] Combat load weight: plates, ammo and water slow you, tire you sooner, and make climbing harder
- [ ] Stamina and heart rate: sprints run out, aim shakes after running, recovers in cover
- [x] Ammo counting by the round, not by the mag: partial mags kept, consolidated in lulls (every ammo type)
- [ ] Reload types: tactical (keep the mag) vs speed (drop it), chosen by the situation
- [ ] Weapon malfunctions by condition and round count; dirt and water raise the odds
- [ ] Hearing: gunfire indoors deafens without ear pro; ear pro on the elite and pro classes
- [ ] Muzzle blast and flash give away position; suppressors cut both
- [ ] Ballistic dispersion by ammo lot and barrel heat; first-round cold-bore shift for snipers
- [ ] Wind that varies along the bullet's path (valleys, buildings), shown only by flags, grass and mirage
- [ ] Range estimation errors that depend on optics and terrain (dead ground, haze)
- [ ] Spotting: muzzle flash at night, silhouettes on ridgelines, movement against the background
- [ ] Night: no NVG means real darkness; NVG halos at lights; thermal blinded by fire
- [ ] Body armor coverage by actual plate size (10 x 12 in front plate), side plates, plate angles
- [ ] Helmet deflection at shallow angles; ricochets off helmets
- [ ] Shock and awe: flashbang effects by distance and facing, temporary deafness and blindness ✓ partly
- [ ] Fragmentation patterns that leave shadows behind cover and lying flat helps ✓ partly
- [ ] Blast overpressure worse indoors (rooms amplify)
- [ ] Bullet penetration through multiple people ✓ and through vehicle doors ✓; tires and engines to add
- [ ] Casualty evacuation to a collection point; triage by priority; tourniquet conversion
- [ ] Morale by team: leader killed, buddy killed, flanked, out of ammo; breaking and running
- [ ] Surrender and detainee handling: cuffs, search, guard
- [ ] Rules of engagement: hostile intent, civilians, escalation of force
- [ ] Communication delays: radio calls take time, can be jammed; hand signals when quiet
- [ ] Fog of war on the enemy too: they report and act on what they actually saw ✓
- [ ] Doors that stick, open inward or outward, locked from one side
- [x] Stairs that slow movement and are deadly to fight on
- [ ] Shooting from inside rooms at windows (staying back from the opening) ✓ cover rules
- [ ] Wet and cold: hypothermia in water, rain slows everything a little
- [ ] Day length, dawn and dusk light levels shifting during a mission
- [ ] Snow and mud tracks the enemy can follow ✓ footprints, AI tracking to add
- [ ] Vehicle sound carrying far; engines heard before seen
- [ ] Drones: battery in cold, signal loss behind hills, operators found by direction-finding

cards.title: backlog: vehicle roadmap
cards.body:
from docs/BACKLOG.md (Vehicle roadmap). 5 of 15 already in the game.

- [x] Hatchback and SUV, gears, slip, backfires, seats, firing ports by window
- [x] Enemy vehicle patrols that dismount on contact
- [x] Pickup with a mounted machine gun (technical), with a gunner seat that turns
- [ ] Armored SUV: doors and glass that stop pistol and rifle rounds, heavier and slower
- [ ] Light armored vehicle (MRAP) with a remote weapon station; immune to small arms, not to charges
- [ ] Vehicle damage model: ✓ tires shot flat, radiators, engines, fuel leaks and fuel fires; crew wounds from spall to add
- [ ] Convoys: column driving with spacing, react to contact drills (push through, dismount, reverse)
- [ ] Ambush drills for the player's convoys: the AI driver accelerates out of the kill zone
- [ ] Road network and navigation for vehicles separate from foot paths; traffic for city maps
- [ ] Checkpoints: stop, search, vehicle-borne threat
- [x] Headlights and blackout driving at night; driving on NVG
- [ ] Vehicle sounds: engines by model, gear changes, horn, door slams
- [x] Ramming doors and fences (there are no gates to ram yet: they're gaps); breaching a wall with a truck to add
- [ ] Boats on the valley river; fording depth by vehicle height
- [ ] Helicopters (insertion, extraction, a door gunner), much later
